meta.overview: Mechanics & Formatting Rules for Chewy copy. Covers capitalization, punctuation, numbers, special characters, word choice, and structure. Intended for a Copy Checker GPT to detect and explain mechanical/style issues and suggest compliant rewrites.
meta.notes: Expanded with rich examples. Use alongside the brand file for full coverage.

capitalization.description: Headlines, subcopy, subject lines, eyebrows, and CTAs use sentence case. Capitalize only the first word and proper nouns.

do: Headline: Litter that clumps how kitty likes
CTA: Shop dry food
Subject: Flea & tick answers, right when you need them
dont: Headline: Litter That Clumps How Kitty Likes
CTA: SHOP DRY FOOD
Subject: Flea & Tick Answers, Right When You Need Them.

capitalization.suggestion: Convert to sentence case; remove ending period in headlines; keep proper nouns capitalized.

capitalization.description: Capitalize names (people, pets), product names, and Chewy programs. Treat true shopping categories as proper nouns in nav/headers/CTAs; use discretion in body copy.

do: Explore Fresh & Prepared recipes your dog will daydream about.
See what’s new in Flea & Tick.
Shop Dry Food.
dont: Explore fresh & prepared recipes your dog will daydream about.
See what’s new in flea & tick.
Shop dry food. (in a nav/CTA context)

capitalization.suggestion: Capitalize category names in navigation, headers, CTAs; lowercase when used descriptively in running text.

capitalization.description: Do not use ALL CAPS for emphasis. All-caps brand-mandated stylings and abbreviations are exceptions (e.g., DNA, LLC, KONG).

do: Get 25% off select toys
Meet KONG classics your pup can’t put down
dont: GET 25% OFF SELECT TOYS
Meet Kong classics your pup can’t put down

capitalization.suggestion: Use font weight, layout, or phrasing for emphasis; keep exceptions properly capitalized.

punctuation.description: Do not use periods at the end of headlines unless the headline contains multiple full sentences.

do: Long walks ahead
No more fleas. No more ticks.
dont: Long walks ahead.
The right leash makes together time even better.

punctuation.suggestion: Remove trailing period in headlines unless you have multiple complete sentences.

punctuation.description: Subcopy takes ending punctuation for complete thoughts.

do: Big on pets not on prices.
Save on everything they love and need.
dont: Big on pets not on prices
Save on everything they love & need

punctuation.suggestion: Add a period to finish the subcopy; use 'and' unless '&' is part of a set style.

punctuation.description: Use the Oxford comma in series of three or more items. If an ampersand replaces 'and', do not use the Oxford comma before '&'.

do: Cats love treats, catnip, and cozy naps.
Cats love treats, catnip & cozy naps.
dont: Cats love treats, catnip and cozy naps.
Cats love treats, catnip, & cozy naps.

punctuation.suggestion: Add the final comma in lists of three or more unless using an ampersand as a stylistic connector.

punctuation.description: Colons introduce emphasis/lists; capitalize next word if it starts a full sentence. Semicolons link related clauses or complex lists. Em dashes create emphasis or asides; use sparingly in long-form.

do: Set them up right: Pick a harness they’ll love.
This toy gets squeaks, tugs, and zoomies—without ripping.
dont: Set them up right - pick a harness they’ll love.
This toy gets squeaks — without ripping. (spaces around em dash in running text)

punctuation.suggestion: Use true em dashes (—) without spaces in running text; prefer colon for simple emphasis.

punctuation.description: Avoid ellipses in headlines; reserve for social/scripts to indicate a pause. Periods/commas go inside quotes. Parenthetical punctuation goes outside unless the parenthetical is a full sentence.

do: “Hey, is that your Yorkie’s name?” she asked.
Gear for your daily walk (okay, your dog’s daily walk).
dont: Long walks ahead...
Gear for your daily walk. (okay, your dog’s daily walk)

punctuation.suggestion: Replace ellipses with stronger phrasing; check quote and parenthesis punctuation placement.

numbers.description: Spell out one through nine; use numerals for 10 and above. Spell out numbers at the start of a sentence.

do: Six chews your heavy chewer can’t put down.
Save on 12-lb bags for bigger appetites.
dont: 6 chews your heavy chewer can’t put down.
Twelve-lb bags for bigger appetites.

numbers.suggestion: Spell 1–9; switch to numerals 10+; never start a sentence with numerals.

numbers.description: Dates: Month D, YYYY (Dec 1). No superscripts (1st). Times: use a.m./p.m. with periods; may remove periods when space is tight.

do: Sale starts Dec 1.
Your vet call is at 3 p.m.
dont: Sale starts December 1st.
Your vet call is at 3 PM.

numbers.suggestion: Drop superscripts; prefer ‘a.m.’/‘p.m.’; allow compact forms when constrained.

numbers.description: Measurements: use numerals (1 oz, 12 cups). Percentages: numerals with no space before % (25%). Keep decimals to two places max; use leading 0 for <1.

do: Serve 1 oz daily for adult cats.
Save 25% when you spend $100 on select food.
dont: Serve one oz daily for adult cats.
Save 25 % when you spend $100 on select food.

numbers.suggestion: Use numerals for measurements; write ‘25%’, not ‘25 %’; keep decimals tidy.

special_characters.description: Use ‘&’ only in banners or associated assets. Avoid in long-form, PDPs, DIM long descriptions, or legal.

do: Treats, toys & more (banner)
dont: Treats, toys & more. (body copy)

special_characters.description: Use the plus sign with numbers (e.g., $49+). Don’t replace the words ‘and’ or ‘plus’. Prefer ‘over’ unless space is limited.

do: Free shipping on orders $49+.
dont: Join Autoship + get free shipping.

special_characters.suggestion: Use ‘and’ instead of ‘+’ between words unless indicating numeric thresholds.

special_characters.description: No underline or strikethrough. Italics only in special cases (e.g., film titles on PDP).

do: Award-winning *The Dogfather* (film) featured this breed.
dont: Award-winning The Dogfather featured this breed. (needs italics)
~Save now~  (strikethrough)

special_characters.suggestion: Avoid underline/strikethrough; use italics sparingly when referencing titles.

word_choice.description: Capitalize Autoship; do not verb it. Use ‘repeat orders’/‘automatic refills’ instead of ‘subscription’.

do: Save on your first Autoship order.
Set up repeat orders to never run out.
dont: Save on your first autoship order.
Subscribe to food deliveries.

word_choice.suggestion: Capitalize Autoship; replace ‘subscription’ with ‘repeat orders’ or ‘automatic refills’.

word_choice.description: Avoid clichés, pet puns, vague hype, finance/business jargon, and sensitive/ableist terms.

do: Make bath day easier with a no-slip mat and gentle suds.
Get more of what they love, without overspending.
dont: Paw-some deals that are the best in the universe!
Crushing it with ROI on your pet spend.

word_choice.suggestion: Use concrete, respectful language; celebrate value without hype or jargon.

word_choice.description: Use ‘cart’, not ‘basket’ or ‘bag’, when referring to checkout.

do: Add to cart
dont: Add to basket
Add to bag

structure.description: Use headline + subcopy or headline-only. Subcopy-only is not an option. Headlines grab attention; subcopy adds brief context.

do:
Headline: Favorite litter
Subcopy: Clumps how kitty likes.
Headline: Litter that clumps how kitty likes
dont: Subcopy: Clumps how kitty likes.

structure.suggestion: Add a concise headline or fold the subcopy into a single, clear headline.

structure.description: Sentence fragments are okay when clear, especially in headlines and subcopy.

do: Fresh toys for marathon chewers.
For the cat who never met a sunbeam they didn't like.
dont: Run-on fragments that confuse meaning and bury the CTA

structure.suggestion: Keep fragments crisp and meaningful; avoid stacking fragments that obscure the message.
